newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks edge up, but market stagnant.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks edge up, but market stagnant.

text.p: Trading flagged on the Cyprus Stock Exchange during the week ending Friday as it hovered at low levels which were seen consolidating, market watchers said.
"It is a stagnant market with a marginal change," said Christodoulos Ellinas, partner at Share Link stockbrokers in Nicosia.
"People should understand that this is the best of a buyers market," he added, suggesting that some buyers were still waiting on the sidelines for prices to sink further.
"They should not wait for it to reach a bottom because we don't know what, or when, that bottom will be."
The CSE index nudged up 0.25 percent to close at 74.90 points in the week ending on Friday, from 74.71 last week. The market trades in 89 securities of 43 listed companies.
"There is a bear trend on the market," said another analyst. "Volumes are depressed because of the summer period and the pressure on prices has risen."
Banking shares closed 0.57 percent up at 84.00 points from 83.52 last week.
Shares in the Bank of Cyprus (Investments) went up one cent to close at 294.5. Shares in the Cyprus Popular Bank closed Friday at 299, 2.5 cents higher than last week.
Part-dividend shares of the same bank were trading three cents up at 297.5.
Hellenic Bank fully paid shares closed the week at 283, 3.5 cents higher than last Friday while Universal Bank shares slipped 3.5 cents to close at 187.5.
Insurance company stocks fell 1.9 percent to close at 56.45 points.
Shares in the Universal Life Insurance company fell 17.5 cents to 450.5, after a 13 cent rise recorded during the previous week. Paneuropean shares slipped one cent to close at 97.5.
Interamerican Insurance fully paid shares were trading at 85.5, 1.5 cents lower than last week.
Retailing chain Woolworth was trading at 64.5 cents, down one cent from last week. Import company Cyprus Trading Corporation, shed half a cent, closing at 103.
Blue chip cement stocks Vassiliko fully paid dropped half a cent to 151, its partly paid also half a cent to 122 and Cyprus Cement retreated three cents to 226.5.
Beer and wine manufacturer KEO shares added one cent, closing at 104.5
Shares in national carrier Cyprus Airways were trading at 34.5 cents from 34.7 cents last week.
